html:
After a gunman killed 35 people at the Port Arthur historic site in Tasmania on 28 April 1996, Australia's governments agreed within weeks on the National Firearms Agreement, banning most automatic and semi-automatic guns.

Prime Minister John Howard pushed it through despite anger in rural areas. A buyback destroyed several hundred thousand guns.

Australia has had far fewer mass shootings since, and the law is often cited in debates abroad. New Zealand made a similar ban after 2019. The site, once a convict prison, is now a memorial. See Australia.
